name: document-workspace
title: Document Workspace
description: A notes or docs workspace: an explorer, tabs, breadcrumb, toolbar, the document (edit or read), an aside for backlinks, properties and the outline, a status bar with the save state, an alert slot and Ctrl/Cmd+P quick open. Resizable, collapsible columns when its container is wide, drawers when narrow; named landmarks and toggles agents can press. Also DocumentOutline and DocumentQuickOpen.
docs: `<DocumentWorkspace document={mode === "edit" ? <MarkdownEditor ref={editor} …/> : <MarkdownView …/>} explorer tabs breadcrumb toolbar statusBar aside alert quickOpen={<DocumentQuickOpen items onOpen />} mode onModeChange editorRef={editor} headings={extractHeadings(markdown)} saveState storageKey>`. It fills its parent (`--document-workspace-height`, 100% by default) and decides its layout from its own width, never the viewport, so it works inside an app shell's `<main>` (in a `Shell`, give it `main="fill"` or the route `main: "fill"` and it fills the height left): at `narrow` (760 px) or less, the explorer and the aside are 20rem drawers that start closed; wider, they are resizable columns (`Resize files`, `Resize details` handles) that collapse from their toggles or the handle. `explorerOpen`/`onExplorerOpenChange` and `asideOpen`/`onAsideOpenChange` follow what is shown; turning narrow closes them and turning wide brings back the columns. `storageKey` remembers the columns' state and widths in localStorage (the drawers always start closed). Landmarks: the explorer is a `nav`, the aside an `aside`, the document a named region (`documentAs="main"` when the workspace is the page's main content); the toggles carry `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`. The mode switch is a SegmentedControl; switching keeps the reading position by heading (from the editor's `getScrollLine` to the read view's headings and back). `saveState` (`saved`, `saving`, `unsaved`, `error`) is a polite `<output>` in the status bar; `alert` sits in an assertive region that is always there, so a conflict is read once when it appears (pass an `Alert` without `live`). `quickOpen` adds a Quick open button and `quickOpenShortcut` (`mod+p`, `false` to turn it off). `DocumentOutline` lists `headings`: in edit mode an entry puts the caret at the heading (`setSelection`, `scrollToLine`) and focuses the editor; in read mode it scrolls to the heading and focuses it. Drawers, quick open and menus give focus back to the document unless the action moved it: pass `useDocumentWorkspace().documentFocusTarget` as `finalFocus` to your own menus in `toolbar`. `editorRef` takes any `DocumentEditor` (`focus`, `scrollToLine`, `setSelection`, `getScrollLine`), which `MarkdownEditorHandle` is. All text is in `labels`.
